title: Witness robustness: An operational quantifier of measurement resources via free state discrimination
authors: Jingsong Ao, Aby Philip, Alexander Streltsov
abstract: We introduce the witness robustness of quantum measurements, a resource quantifier whose admissible noise consists of tuples of free-state witnesses rather than physical measurements. We establish its operational interpretation: it quantifies the maximal advantage that a measurement can provide over free measurements in discriminating an ensemble composed entirely of free states. Unlike the standard and generalized robustnesses, the witness robustness is not faithful in general, reflecting the fact that a resourceful measurement need not be useful when only free states can be prepared. We identify conditions under which faithfulness is recovered and show that, in resource theories admitting a resource-destroying map, the witness robustness vanishes for every measurement. We also establish fundamental properties, including convexity and monotonicity. Finally, we derive analytical results for projective measurements in single-qubit magic and for binary pure-state projective measurements in the two-qubit PPT entanglement theory.
summary: This paper develops the concept of 'witness robustness' to quantify how much a quantum measurement exceeds what is achievable using only 'free states.' It establishes this measure through an operational interpretation based on discrimination success probabilities. This provides a powerful, generalized tool for resource quantification in quantum information theory.
main_problem: The paper introduces and characterizes 'witness robustness' as a novel resource quantifier for quantum measurements, designed to measure the advantage of a measurement over free measurements.
main_result: Witness robustness quantifies the maximal advantage in discriminating an ensemble of only free states. It is shown that this measure is not always faithful but provides a direct operational characterization via success probabilities in discrimination games.
method: The authors define witness robustness by considering noise drawn from the dual cone of free states (free-state witnesses), leading to an infimum minimization problem solved using minimax theorems.
model_or_system: The framework is general quantum information theory, analyzing measurements ($M$) within a resource theory context defined by a set of 'free states' ($F$). Specific applications include single-qubit magic and two-qubit PPT entanglement.
key_observables: Witness robustness ($	ext{RF}_{	ext{MF}}(M)$), success probabilities in state discrimination games, and various forms of generalized/standard robustness measures.
important_parameters: The geometry of the free state set ($F$) dictates the behavior of the resource measure; the analysis compares different norms (e.g., $\ell_\infty$ vs. Euclidean).
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that noise can be modeled by tuples of free-state witnesses, which relaxes constraints compared to standard robustness measures.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates how witness robustness mixes the measurement $M$ with a tuple of witnesses $W$, showing the relationship between different sets defining the resource measure.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first introducing the concept, establishing its operational interpretation via discrimination games (Theorem 1), deriving fundamental properties like convexity and monotonicity, and concluding with analytical results for specific physical examples.
why_interesting: It provides a sophisticated, generalized tool to quantify resource advantages in quantum tasks where standard measures fail due to limitations on state preparation or noise modeling.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Witness robustness as a relaxation of the admixed noise. All sets live in the space of N-tuples of observables: the free measurements MF sit inside all measurements M, both bounded convex sets, which in turn sit inside the unbounded product cone [cone∗(F)]×N of witness tuples—tuples W = {Wi} whose every component is a free-state witness—with apex at the zero tuple 0. The witness robustness mixes the resourceful target M with such a tuple W—not with another measurement—until the convex combination (M + rW)/(1 + r) first meets MF; the least weight r is RF MF(M). Restricting the noise instead to M or to MF recovers the generalized and standard robustness, so that RF MF ≤RMF ≤Rstd MF .
